verify.description: Checks a list of factual claims about the code against the repository, read-only, and returns verdicts with evidence. Use it on a draft before giving a factual answer to the user.

check.description: The verifier as a primary agent for headless runs by scripts/harness/ask.py; hidden from the window.

editor.description: Writes the planned change for /custom-graph-build in headless runs: only the planned files, no commands; hidden from the window.

graph.description: Runs a question through the coded graph for /custom-graph and shows the checked answer; hidden from the window.

verify.description: check the factual claims of the last answer against the repository
verify.template: Verify your last answer. 1. List every factual claim in it as numbered lines: counts, names, acronym expansions, descriptions of components, mechanisms, file paths. 2. Call the verify subagent with the task tool (subagent_type "verify") and give it the numbered list and the project directory; ask it for the verdict table. 3. Show its table, then give the corrected answer with every corrected claim marked. $ARGUMENTS

ask.description: answer a question in four steps: narrow questions, one explore subagent each, verify, compose
ask.template: Answer the question at the end in four steps and show each step. 1. Write the narrow factual questions behind it, 3 to 12, each answerable by one command or one file. 2. For each question call the task tool with subagent_type "explore" and that question alone; keep its evidence table. 3. Call the task tool with subagent_type "verify" with the numbered question and answer pairs and the project directory; show its verdict table. 4. Write the answer from the verified pairs only, citing them by number; where the pairs do not cover a part of the question, write "not checked". Question: $ARGUMENTS

custom-graph.description: answer a question with the coded graph: narrow questions in fresh sessions, every answer checked, then composed (6 to 30 minutes)
custom-graph.template:
Answer the question between the markers with the custom_graph tool, then reply with its output exactly as returned.
<question>
$ARGUMENTS
</question>

custom-graph-build.description: plan a change with the coded graph and show the plan; /custom-graph-build go then makes it: one editor, the project's build and test, at most 2 fix rounds, a checker (10 to 60 minutes)
custom-graph-build.template:
Run the request between the markers through the custom_graph tool, then reply with its output exactly as returned.
<mode>build</mode>
<question>
$ARGUMENTS
</question>

remember.description: save one fact about this project to its notes (asks you before writing)
remember.template:
Save one fact about this project to its notes. The owner is telling you this fact: save it as given, without checking it first, unless the files clearly contradict it (then say what you found instead). Rewrite it as one short sentence that stands on its own: name the file, command or component instead of writing 'it' or 'this'. Then run exactly one command: agent-notes add "<the sentence>" . The owner is asked to approve that command before it runs. Do not edit any file. If the command answers that the entry is already there or the notes are full, tell the owner and stop.

Fact: $ARGUMENTS
